# AI coding reliability guide

Use this guide before implementing or reviewing a change, especially a bug fix,
refactor, merge resolution or optimization. Its purpose is to turn recurring
failure modes into concrete design questions and executable checks. Compiling,
adding a timeout or passing a happy-path test does not establish reliability.

This guide owns the cross-cutting review method and reusable failure patterns.
[Module ownership](module-boundaries.md) owns implementation boundaries;
[architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md), [network contracts](network-design-reference.md)
and feature guides own behavior and resource limits. The
[testing workflow](testing-feedback-loop.md) owns commands, selection and gates.
Link to those owners instead of copying their changing contracts here. When code
and a contract disagree, resolve the intended behavior rather than documenting
the regression as the new rule.

## Use on every change

1. **Locate the owner and consumers.** Read the owning implementation, callers,
   existing tests and relevant guide before adding another helper or state owner.
   Include callbacks, IPC handlers, retries, startup, shutdown and recovery paths;
   an import graph alone cannot reveal all consumers.
2. **State the invariant and select risks.** Describe what must remain true on
   success, failure, cancellation and replacement. Use the table below to select
   applicable rules. A small diff can change lock order or lifetime semantics.
3. **Trace the failure path before editing.** For concurrency work, sketch who
   owns each lock, permit, task and mutable state; what it waits for; and who
   releases it. For a reproducible bug, construct a focused failing regression.
   Record unresolved hypotheses as hypotheses, not confirmed defects.
4. **Implement at the existing boundary.** Preserve authority, durable acceptance,
   compatibility and resource budgets. Recheck invariants after moving work
   outside a guard. Evaluate the proposed fix for new races and deadlocks too.
5. **Verify the changed boundary and report evidence.** Run affected checks and
   required boundary scenarios under the testing workflow. Explain results,
   exclusions and unresolved evidence. Update this guide when the defect exposes
   a reusable failure pattern; follow the maintenance procedure below.

Keep the risk explanation proportional to the change. A documentation edit does
not require a new concurrency test. A changed async callback does require a
lifetime review even when the diff is one line. Put task-specific reasoning and
results in the PR or ignored local evidence, not a new permanent report.

## Select rules by the changed boundary

| Change or symptom                                                        | Read at least                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Locks, callbacks, synchronous dispatch, UI freezes                       | [R01](#r01-lock-order-and-reentrant-calls), [R02](#r02-thread-and-scheduler-progress), [R10](#r10-evidence-that-exercises-the-failure)                |
| Background work, native providers, logout, shutdown or cancellation      | [R02](#r02-thread-and-scheduler-progress), [R03](#r03-actual-work-owns-its-lifetime), [R06](#r06-exact-authority-and-stale-completions)               |
| Network requests, retries, polling, queues or batches                    | [R03](#r03-actual-work-owns-its-lifetime), [R04](#r04-deadlines-cover-the-whole-operation), [R05](#r05-bounded-work-must-also-make-progress)          |
| React effects, IPC reads, dialogs, optimistic updates or mutation status | [R06](#r06-exact-authority-and-stale-completions), [R07](#r07-observation-is-not-mutation-ownership), [R10](#r10-evidence-that-exercises-the-failure) |
| Storage, settings, imports, deletion or recovery                         | [R06](#r06-exact-authority-and-stale-completions), [R08](#r08-durable-state-and-failure-semantics), [R09](#r09-bound-input-and-resource-use)          |
| IPC/API inputs, files, media or protocol changes                         | [R06](#r06-exact-authority-and-stale-completions), [R08](#r08-durable-state-and-failure-semantics), [R09](#r09-bound-input-and-resource-use)          |
| Merge resolution, shared helper or dependency changes                    | Revisit the affected callers and all applicable rules; a clean textual merge does not establish compatible ownership or semantics.                    |

These are starting points, not permission to ignore another reachable boundary.
Do not add a global lock, retry loop, timeout or shared abstraction solely to make
the local symptom disappear.

A frozen UI may result from a lock cycle, blocked event thread, starvation, lost
wakeup, unbounded work or stale loading state. Identify the mechanism and the
missing progress condition before selecting a fix; these need different evidence.

## R01: Lock order and reentrant calls

**Failure pattern:** one path takes A then B while another takes B then A; or a
helper/callback reacquires a nonrecursive lock its caller already holds. The
second case can deadlock on a single thread. Nested reads also need review when
a queued writer can prevent a new read from completing.

Trace actual acquisition order through callees, authorization callbacks,
destructors and error cleanup. Include main-thread dispatch and task joins as
wait dependencies, not just mutexes. A typical UI cycle is:

```text
background task: holds session guard -> waits for main-thread callback
main thread:     handles UI event    -> waits for session guard
```

Use the owning module's order; do not invent one universal order for unrelated
subsystems. Make whether a helper acquires a guard or requires one explicit.
Avoid invoking arbitrary callbacks while guarded. Where a commit callback must
run inside an authority guard, keep that contract narrow and inspect its complete
call chain. Queue presentation without retaining a guard needed by the UI;
validate captured authority when the queued callback executes.

**Evidence:** exercise both competing paths and the real authorization variant.
An ordinary admission fixture does not cover a sensitive proof that itself locks
app state. Assert that the other operation progresses, not just that the first
eventually returns. See `checked_at_lock_revision` in
[runtime admission](../src-tauri/src/runtime_admission.rs), the verified-login
regression in [shared login tests](../src-tauri/src/shared_account_login/tests.rs),
and queued notification tests in [runtime state](../src-tauri/src/chat_commands/state.rs).

scheduler awaits optional work before polling unrelated ready operations.

signature. Move blocking work through the existing admitted worker boundary.
Inspect React render/effect/subscriber feedback loops and large synchronous data
transforms too; moving I/O off the UI thread does not bound those CPU costs.
Prepare bulk data outside shared commit guards, then reacquire the required
guards and revalidate before atomic publication. Keep critical sections small
without splitting a transaction or permitting stale side effects. Replacing a
mutex with an async mutex alone does not repair ownership or lock order.

Check that the UI event loop, accept loop and control scheduler can still make
progress while the worker is paused. Offloading a scan does not help other
branches of a scheduler if that scheduler still waits for the entire scan inside
one completion branch. Synchronous final persistence can still block; document
that boundary instead of claiming a timer can preempt it.

blocked branch poll another branch of that same future. Independently scheduled

just to exercise scheduling. Keep real scanner acceptance in its existing job.
Exercise interrupted log finalization as well as child retirement through the
existing [process-owner controls](ai-coding-reliability.md#r03-actual-work-owns-its-lifetime).
Compare nested budgets before adding an outer subprocess timeout: several valid
inner probes can exhaust it before the behavior under test starts. A passing PR
run cannot qualify an unbounded environmental dependency for later main runs.
Do not use a fixed sleep to infer that background synchronization has happened.
Bind negative assertions to an actual post-change operation: for deletion replay,
prove the erased record was offered again and all pages were applied before
checking that it remains absent. A successful page, unchanged-digest response or
unrelated worker notification does not prove a complete replay. Keep deadlines
as failure bounds, and retain ownership and joins for admitted work on timeout.
Request that work through its existing coordinator and observe its publication
revision and terminal completion. A second hand-driven page loop can race the
normal worker and bypass its serialization, recovery and cancellation contract.
Capture immutable precondition evidence before admitting an operation that can
invalidate it. Published projections may legitimately become pending during a
commit; a post-admission read cannot prove the operation's initial role. Wait on
the existing preparation owner within the original setup deadline and fail
unexpected errors instead of retrying the whole operation.
Give counterfactual source copies their own Cargo target directory. Relative
package paths can collide across copies and reuse a mutated test executable;
the canonical candidate must never consume a negative control's build output.
Asynchronous progress notifications are observations, not readiness barriers. Cancellation
fixtures must bind readiness to still-live owned work after the required real
materialization, then assert its retirement before later admission or cleanup;
a bounded fallback may fail missing readiness but cannot manufacture a pass.

Executable fixtures must own an independent copied image, not a hard link to
the running test harness. Assert file identity before launch. After verified
process retirement, use the shared bounded filesystem cleanup helper; persistent
locks must still fail. Keep the Windows held-image failure and release controls
in `release-reuse.test.mjs`; cleanup retries never retry the test assertion or
substitute for process retirement.

Git-path and mode controls should construct Git objects when the host cannot
represent the input faithfully. Assert the actual delta and mode before checking
rejection; an empty change rejected for another reason is not a valid negative
control. Keep these cases on every platform instead of skipping them.

Browser commands use the existing process owner with a deadline inside the total
job budget, reserving time for joined cleanup and evidence upload. Keep streamed
logs and append-only active/completed-case progress when final reports cannot be
written. Timeout or uncertain cleanup remains a failure. Preserve verified closure of owned work as a diagnostic separately from the
actual child outcome: Windows
intentionally terminates even an empty job to close descendant admission.
On POSIX, verify the framework's independently grouped web server as well as the
CLI group. Use its supported graceful interruption protocol; a missing teardown
acknowledgment means cleanup remains unverified. Bind lifecycle markers to the
current invocation so old evidence cannot prove a later process stopped.
Do not await output-pipe closure indefinitely after the command leader exits.
The existing process owner bounds draining after group retirement; a separately
grouped descendant retaining stdout or stderr must yield a failed structured
result with unverified cleanup and a quarantined lease. Closing owned read ends
does not prove the escaped process stopped. Keep real natural-exit, cancellation
and no-success-receipt controls rather than signalling unknown process groups.
Authorize PID cleanup only from a complete private acknowledgment, not a numeric
prefix in a stdout chunk. Stream reads do not preserve message boundaries; a
failed readiness publication must retire the child through its creation owner.
Actual CLI regression fixtures need private output directories as well as private
source directories; parallel Playwright commands otherwise delete one another's
traces and manufacture failures. Missing hosted logs do not identify a slow case.
Local-only evidence fixtures must explicitly isolate and restore inherited CI
flags, and separately assert that real CI cannot reuse local acceptance evidence.
Health captures its absolute budget before setup and uses the existing stage
owner to stop diagnostics before the job watchdog. Preserve its structured result,
execution log and bounded Node lifecycle records, including the active file/case,
through the always-upload path. Prove interruption and joined cleanup with a real
parked command. Missing hosted logs require better evidence, not a guessed fix.
Cancellation during preparation still needs a failed structured result. Only the
command owner can attest that admission never happened; failures after that
boundary must retain uncertain cleanup rather than manufacture a no-work result.

The [fixture timing guidance](testing-feedback-loop.md#cold-fixture-preparation-versus-measured-progress)
owns concrete examples and permitted boundaries.

Prefer bounded condition waits and meaningful failure diagnostics. Browser
actions should use [Playwright actionability and retrying assertions](https://playwright.dev/docs/actionability)
where applicable; application readiness may still need its own signal. Arbitrary
sleeps, broader timeouts, blanket retries and weaker assertions need evidence;
they are not default repairs for an unexplained failure. If a narrowly scoped
infrastructure retry is justified, keep its limit, original failure and outcomes
visible, and ensure repeating the operation is safe. Test retries still obey the
owning suite policy.

When a UI action moves into a menu, update the existing shared interaction helper
and its callers before publication. Exercise the real entry point; retain
functional, permission, focus and geometry assertions at the toolbar or popup
boundary they describe. The
[composer attachment helper](../frontend/e2e/helpers/session.ts) owns that shared
interaction; forced visibility and dropped assertions do not qualify the new flow.

Keep each observation inside a polling assertion nonwaiting when the assertion
already owns readiness. A locator operation can wait for a virtualized row and
consume the entire outer budget without producing one decode or geometry sample.
Inspect the trace to distinguish missing samples from unequal values; use one
browser-side DOM snapshot, treating an absent row as pending. Establish visible
fixture preparation before releasing held media bytes and starting decode checks.
Preserve exact geometry and cache assertions, and exercise the absent-row control
with a snapshot-only observer rather than extending the deadline. The media-scroll
remount regression owns this case. Run independent adversarial sampler controls
after the cache-remount journey, so they cannot consume its retention window.

For a reproducible race or timeout fix, use a regression or negative control that
fails for the original mechanism and passes with the repair. Confirm that the
intended case actually ran. Preserve existing coverage while investigating; any
temporary quarantine needs an explicit owner, reason, tracking issue and removal
condition under the existing gate policy.

## Reject incomplete discovery and generated-policy drift

Successful test execution requires successful, complete input discovery.
`scripts/ci/fuzz-targets.py` compares the discovered cargo-fuzz list with the actual
manifest-owned target inventory before running anything. Failed enumeration, an
empty list, duplicates, omissions or unknown targets fail the job, as do individual
target failures. Keep this assertion at the execution owner; shell loop command
substitution alone does not propagate discovery failure under `set -e`.

`scripts/ci/glib-migration.py` evaluates every resolved glib branch, rather than
treating a newer parallel branch as proof that an older stack was removed. Its
migration claim conservatively requires stable 0.20 or newer throughout; absent
glib and mixed old/new trees do not establish migration. The
[RustSec advisory](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2024-0429.html) owns the
security version ranges; the watcher retains native build/test and reviewed-PR
requirements before changing dependencies.

Generated native input probes share one accepted-key/extended-flag metadata owner
between WebDriver mapping and emitted C# policy. Regressions must check that every
emitted key is accepted with the correct flags and unsupported keys remain
rejected, rather than only matching the generated call text. Ownership checks and
real desktop acceptance remain separate from generator/compilation checks.

## Review the change and prevent renewed drift

Follow the existing validation stages; do not invent a parallel completion
process. For changes affecting CI behavior or recurring cost, include the
following in the normal [alignment review](maintenance-checklist.md#review-and-follow-up-procedure):

- The acceptance boundary and retained owner, including consumers affected by
  deletion, merging, selection or schedule changes.
- The measured bottleneck, comparable before/after scope and remaining unknowns;
  distinguish observed latency, resource cost and reliability.
- Executed validation and source identity, with inventory/provenance checks or
  regression controls appropriate to the changed mechanism.
- Remaining hosted, cross-platform, native or release evidence and the owner of
  any follow-up. Do not claim candidate acceptance from local or older results.

Workflow, runner and tool upgrades can change CLI semantics, report formats,
selectors and archive compatibility. Validate affected real tool invocations and
failure paths through the existing diagnostic owners; YAML parsing or unit mocks
alone do not establish the behavior of the installed tool.

Consolidate frontend unit execution through the complete Linux coverage owner
when the ordinary and coverage commands select the same inventory and platform
branches use explicit mocks. Verify that inventory with the actual runner before
removing duplicate OS executions. Retain real browser/native matrices and native
diagnostic fixtures; mocked platform branches do not supply those contracts.
Keep Node/filesystem portability requirements in their owning diagnostics rather
than duplicating the entire frontend unit suite incidentally.

Keep platform-exclusive probes in the required native producer that can execute
them. Universal local selections must not include a file whose entire suite is
skipped on other hosts; preserve the nonempty-test guard and explicit native
escalation instead. Keep workflow wiring assertions in the cheap CI policy
owner, separate from the underlying tool's filesystem/compiler regressions.
Environment-specific cases must also distinguish unsupported local environments
from broken CI configuration. Skip only the new unsupported case, retain the
file's other checks, and declare its native escalation. A declared GitHub Linux
run must reach strict environment validation even when required image inputs are
missing; never turn that misconfiguration into a skip or fabricate hosted inputs.

After pushing, observe the actual hosted candidate until the relevant jobs finish.
Compare before and after setup time, test time, required-check latency and runner
minutes with sample sizes and cache conditions. Inspect first failures and queue
changes, then make another measured pass when evidence identifies remaining waste.
A pushed branch, a local green subset, or a faster isolated step does not establish
an end-to-end speedup. Keep the candidate reviewable and continue in a clean
worktree when unrelated local edits prevent publication; do not discard those
edits or treat them as a reason to stop the optimization.

Revisit timing and failure evidence when a gate becomes slower, starts rerunning,
gains another platform/dependency, or repeatedly exceeds its expected budget.
During existing maintenance reviews, inspect slow cases, duplicated setup,
shard imbalance, cache churn and abandoned temporary exceptions. Retire obsolete
work with its consumers and selectors rather than accumulating permanent layers.

Keep this review proportional: a documentation-only change needs applicable
formatting, links and structural checks, not a new build benchmark. Rules should
be enforceable through existing contracts and diagnostics where practical;
adding this guide does not create a scheduled job or another required check.

## Dependabot development acceptance

The existing exact-merge scope owner, `scripts/ci/docs-scope.mjs`, also admits
isolated npm dependency profiles for same-repository Dependabot bot PRs targeting
`dev`. Both manifests and lockfiles must already exist as regular files. Only
version changes to existing dependency entries qualify; scripts, overrides,
metadata, additions/removals, mixed paths, unmatched lockfile roots and changed
Tauri bindings retain full verification. Lockfile-only updates currently retain
full verification because their consumer boundary has not been qualified.

The `help` profile runs the public help/MCP tests, build and high-severity audit.
The `frontend` profile runs complete unit coverage, lint/types, production build,
built-JavaScript syntax checks, audit, Chromium theme/layout regressions and the
WebKit portable suite. The selected npm workflow independently checks its profile
against the actual merge. The Linux CI collector requires its success; failure,
cancellation, missing output or unexpected skipping cannot qualify. The legacy
`dev` required `verify` context collects the actual platform results. UI matrices
outside these profiles report not applicable, rather than pretending to execute.
Health retains source ownership/hygiene checks, without unrelated Rust or help
security scans blocking an isolated npm update.

Cargo, Actions and native binding updates retain complete acceptance. Main PRs,
merge groups, pushes, schedules, manual runs and release-source checks retain
full verification, apart from the separately qualified prose-only main PR rule.
The direct main/release check policy is unchanged. Do not classify by actor,
branch name, SemVer label or PR title alone. The existing real-Git scope controls
and CI policy fixtures own positive profiles, source/identity rejection and
failed/cancelled/missing selected-check evidence.

Automatic merge additionally requires verified Dependabot metadata for npm
minor/patch updates in these two directories, no Tauri dependency and no reported
maintainer change. Other updates have automatic merge disabled and require manual
review. The privileged metadata workflow never executes PR source; merge enablement
is bound to the event head. Coverage uploads requiring unavailable Dependabot
credentials remain excluded; tests and retained local artifacts are independent
of external coverage publication.

Deploy this policy through a reviewed main change, then align `dev` through a
reviewed integration before refreshing its dependency PRs. Existing `dev`
workflows cannot acquire fixes from main automatically. Preserve current required
checks; any protection migration uses its existing owner. Measure selected hosted
jobs after rollout, recording source, first failures, runner/setup/test time and
cache conditions. Local policy success is not a hosted latency or native claim.

# Repository Guidelines

## Reliability before implementation

- Before implementing, refactoring, fixing or reviewing code, read the
  [AI coding reliability guide](docs/ai-coding-reliability.md), select the rules
  triggered by the changed boundaries, and inspect the owning code and callers.
  For concurrency/lifecycle changes, trace lock order, wait dependencies, actual
  work ownership, cancellation and commit authority before editing.
- Validate the applicable failure and recovery paths, not only the happy path.
  Record concrete evidence and remaining limits; a timeout, successful build or
  passing subset is not proof that UI freezes or all deadlocks are impossible.
- When a confirmed defect exposes a reusable failure pattern, update that guide's
  existing rule or add a distinct rule with its owner and regression evidence.
  Maintain the owning contract and test selectors; keep incident logs out of the guide.

## Project Structure & Module Organization

- Four-crate Rust workspace. `crates/mesh-talk-core/` is the UI-free protocol core (lib
  `mesh_talk_core` + the `mesh-talk-node` CLI bin in `src/bin/`): feature modules `node/`,
  `identity/`, `transport/`, `discovery/`, `eventlog/`, `ratchet/`, `channel/`, `dm.rs`,
  `file/`, `postoffice/`, `storage/`. `src-tauri/` is the Tauri desktop app: entry
  `src/main.rs` → `lib.rs`, IPC glue in `commands.rs` (auth) + `chat_commands/` (messaging)
  - `events.rs`, plus `state.rs`, `tray.rs`, `services/` (auth only).
- `crates/mesh-talk-integrations/` owns scoped local messaging grants, private IPC,
  and the dedicated bot host/admin CLI; `crates/mesh-talk-mcp/` adapts its four
  send/context/status tools to the official MCP SDK. Neither owns mesh crypto.
- Integration/e2e suites live in `crates/mesh-talk-core/tests/` (`two_node_cli`,
  `persistent_history`, `post_office_offline`, `decoder_smoke`); keep unit tests inline via
  `mod tests` (e.g. `node/node_tests.rs`).
- React client sits in `frontend/src`; Vite tooling in `frontend/package.json`.
- Operational scripts in `scripts/` (`setup-hooks.sh`, `check-health.sh`); architecture in
  `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`; conventions in `specifications/`. The
  [documentation map](docs/README.md) routes readers to maintained guides; the
  [documentation guidelines](docs/DOCUMENTATION_GUIDELINES.md) define ownership
  across the README, guides, and project site.

## Build, Test, and Development Commands

- `make dev` primes Rust + Node deps and installs git hooks.
- `make build` / `make frontend-build` — release build / Vite production build.
- During feature development, preview changed-boundary validation with `make test-plan`
  and run it with `make test-changed`. Unmapped changes require an explicit owner
  and reason; inspect escalation notes for browser/native or consumer checks.
  Use `make verify-plan` / `make verify-changed` at task completion to compose the
  same affected tests with applicable formatting, lint/types and builds. The
  test-only commands do not include static checks; neither mode replaces required
  PR/review, browser/native or release gates. `make validation-report` separates
  queue and execution costs; `make validation-audit` compares a clean affected
  plan with same-source broader failure evidence before narrowing any gate.
  Read selected capability references and inspect pending browser/native requirements.
  Execution prints a structured feedback report; follow the
  [validation protocol](docs/testing-feedback-loop.md#validation-stages-and-agent-responsibilities)
  for completed work, remaining evidence and additive semantic selections.
- During feature development, run affected tests only: `make test-focused
TEST_PACKAGE=mesh-talk-core TEST_FILTER=node::account_sync` selects Rust unit
  tests; add `TEST_TARGET=bridge_cross_lan` to select one integration target.
  `cd frontend && npm test -- src/features/chat/settingsDialogSession.test.ts`
  selects a frontend unit file. `make test` runs the full workspace suite
  (`cargo test --workspace`) for pre-PR and CI gates;
  `make e2e` runs the `#[ignore]`d multi-process backend rigs; `cd frontend && npm run e2e`
  runs the Playwright UI suite. Test builds use cheap KDF params (the `fast-test-kdf`
  feature), and `.cargo/config.toml` caps test/compile parallelism.
- UI / node spot checks: `make tauri-dev`, `make frontend-dev`,
  `cargo run -p mesh-talk-core --bin mesh-talk-node -- --keystore /tmp/a.keystore
--password pw --name alice` (add `--post-office` for relay mode).

## Coding Style & Naming Conventions

- Rust: `cargo fmt` (4-space, `snake_case` modules, `UpperCamelCase` types) +
  **`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`** (must match CI — `--all-targets` covers
  tests/benches).
- Frontend: `npm run format` (Prettier) + `npm run lint` (ESLint flat config).
- Write documentation and reusable prompts in English unless a specific exception is needed.
- Reference `specifications/development_conventions.md` for naming nuances.

## Domain Language

- `CONTEXT.md` is the canonical domain glossary. `docs/domain-design.md` indexes
  the modeling references and defines DDD vocabulary and naming translations.
- Distinguish local users, accounts and devices; desktop, transport and ratchet
  sessions; discovery, presence, custody, recipient delivery and read state.
- Use explicit identity/lifetime names in new code. Preserve public, wire and
  stored identifiers unless a separately validated compatibility change is intended.
- Update the glossary and affected owning guides when a domain meaning changes;
  link to definitions instead of maintaining duplicate glossaries.

## Architecture & Components

- Before adding business logic, consult [module ownership and reuse](docs/module-boundaries.md),
  inspect the owning module and its callers, and extend its existing implementation.
  Parallel tasks should name their owned paths and shared-interface dependencies;
  coordinate changes to shared interfaces through one integration owner. Keep
  feature-specific helpers local and share rules when their meaning and lifecycle
  are the same. The guide owns the detailed assignment and handoff contract.
- Stack: Rust 2024 on Tokio; Tauri 2 + React shell. No vendor-operated server.
- The `Node` (`node/node.rs`) wires identity + signed UDP **multicast** discovery
  (group `224.0.0.167`, port 47474) + Noise-encrypted TCP transport (`transport/`,
  low-level socket in `transport/net.rs`) + the content-addressed event log + DM/channel/
  file crypto. Messages are events synced as a bounded append-only log, account-addressed
  across a user's devices; optional offline custody via equal eligible post offices.
  Routed discovery and opt-in post-office federation connect reachable sites without
  joining their IP subnets. Wire formats are versioned bincode.
- See **`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`** before changing crypto, sync, or transport;
  **`docs/network-design-reference.md`** owns the communication invariants,
  module contracts, resource budgets and topology acceptance boundaries.

## Maintaining standards as requirements change

- Before changing tests, fixtures, dependencies or workflows in ways that affect
  CI cost or reliability, read [CI maintenance](docs/ci-maintenance.md). Reuse
  existing owners, measure the affected cost, and preserve acceptance evidence;
  keep required-check policy in its existing owner.
- Before implementation, identify the existing decision owner, authoritative rule,
  observable acceptance criteria, affected consumers and required boundary evidence.
  Extend the owning implementation and `validation.json`; new business capabilities
  should link their guide and invariants. Explain an unchanged contract in the PR.
- Run `make standards-check` after adding/moving source or changing contracts. It
  checks structural ownership and maintained references, including new files; it
  does not prove assertion quality, semantic completeness or candidate readiness.
  Hooks inspect the working tree, so partially staged commits still need a clean
  committed-candidate check in CI. Frontend dependencies must be installed.
- When CI exposes a local omission or flaky fixture, fix the owning selector, task
  or fixture and add a focused regression. Review timing and selection evidence
  before changing policy. Follow the maintained
  [requirement maintenance loop](docs/testing-feedback-loop.md#maintaining-standards-across-requirements).

## Testing Guidelines

- Integration coverage in `crates/mesh-talk-core/tests/` and `node/node_tests.rs`; embed
  unit tests near the code. Networking/crypto changes ship a loopback integration assertion.
- Backend multi-process E2E via `make e2e` (CI: `e2e-backend.yml`); Playwright UI E2E via
  `cd frontend && npm run e2e` (CI: `e2e-ui.yml`).
- Do not run full suites or E2E automatically during ordinary feature work. Run
  the affected unit or integration tests as changes are made; run E2E and the
  comprehensive health gate on explicit request, for optional full local preparation,
  or in CI.
- See `docs/testing-feedback-loop.md` for selection examples and escalation triggers.
- Document executed validation commands in every PR; ensure `make test` passes
  locally or through its matching CI workspace suite before merge.

## Commit & Pull Request Guidelines

- Before changing product versions or release automation, read [the version lifecycle](docs/updates.md#version-ownership-and-lifecycle).
  Root `Cargo.toml` `[workspace.package].version` is authoritative. Use
  `node scripts/release/version.mjs check|sync|prepare VERSION` (the `VERSION` argument belongs
  to `prepare` only); do not hand-edit generated npm/Cargo lock metadata or introduce another
  version constant. Root private npm metadata is a checked release-tooling projection;
  frontend private metadata is versionless and Tauri inherits Cargo. Never broadly replace
  matching dependency, fixture, history, wire or schema versions. Keep source builds `BASE-dev`,
  Nightlies `BASE-nightly.RUN.ATTEMPT`, official tagged builds `BASE`, and standard SemVer ordering.
- Version/changelog preparation and next-development-target changes use reviewed PRs. Ordinary main
  pushes must not create automatic release proposals or commit-derived product notes. Stable publication
  remains explicit through the existing verified tagged-release workflow; no direct main push,
  public empty release, mutable published tag or gate bypass. Nightly publication requires trusted
  `main` and a target above the latest Stable. Future changes must extend the existing version
  owner, its tests, standards/CI enforcement and capability contracts together; the owning guide
  documents permissions, bot-PR checks, dispatch and recovery requirements. Manual Stable draft
  preparation uses the reviewed exact-version CHANGELOG section and requires exact-source checks
  before creating its immutable tag/draft. The fixed release-history
  migration floor is historical provenance; never advance it during ordinary version bumps.

- Conventional commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`); scopes like `feat(node):` align with
  `specifications/git_standards.md`. Squash WIP; link issues. When asked to merge,
  default to squash merge unless the user explicitly requests another strategy;
  follow the [merge policy](specifications/git_standards.md#pull-request-merge-strategy)
  and current-head required checks.
- Create PRs through `./scripts/create-pr.sh -- <gh pr create options>`.
  The default checks the clean committed candidate, comparison base, argument safety,
  whitespace, cheap affected static checks, ownership blockers, structural standards,
  repository hygiene and applicable verified frontend patch coverage before publication.
  Use `make pr-check` for the same cheap static phase; missing current coverage
  evidence reports its explicit generation command and never starts suites implicitly.
  CI runs after publication; full-scope candidates retain cross-platform execution.
  Only the proven [documentation scope](docs/ci-maintenance.md#documentation-only-pr-scope)
  may omit unrelated product tests. All required checks must pass on the current PR head before merging. Creating a PR does not certify test acceptance.
- To run comprehensive checks locally before publication, use
  `./scripts/create-pr.sh --full-preflight <selectors/specs> -- <gh pr create options>`.
  This invokes `prepare-pr.sh` (platform preflight plus full health). For an existing
  PR, `./scripts/prepare-pr.sh <selectors/specs>` provides the same optional local gate.
  Use Playwright specs relevant to changed frontend behavior and repeated
  `--core-filter` / `--host-filter` / `--integration-filter` / `--mcp-filter` selectors
  for changed Rust crates. Preflight runs selected tests in Linux Docker and through
  SSH to `windows10`; Windows workspaces, caches and temporary data stay on drive D.
  Owning scenario rules add visual specs and require real native evidence for
  lifecycle/discovery changes. Missing environments or empty Rust selections fail
  full preflight. Include `e2e/ui-visual-regression.spec.ts` for theme/layout changes.
  See `docs/testing-feedback-loop.md` for configuration, coverage and plan preview.
  Fetch `origin/main` first if the comparison base is stale.
- Record focused validation and outstanding checks in the PR. Use
  `./scripts/check-health.sh` when comprehensive local evidence is needed; protected
  CI remains required before merge regardless of local results.

## Security & Adjustments

- `./scripts/check-health.sh` chains fmt, Clippy `--all-targets`, ESLint, tests, typos,
  cargo-deny, cargo-machete, gitleaks, shellcheck, audits, and both builds.
- Triage vulnerabilities immediately or document mitigation in the PR.
- If plans shift, update the relevant committed design or architecture docs. Keep
  `docs/superpowers/` and the root `plans/` directory local and untracked.

## Repository Hygiene

### Worktree lifecycle

- Create a worktree only when isolation is needed. Before creating one, inspect
  `git worktree list --porcelain` and record the task-owned path, branch and any
  dedicated build directory in ignored `tmp/` task notes. Treat pre-existing
  worktrees and unrelated changes as user-owned; never sweep them automatically.
- The coordinating session owns cleanup of every worktree it creates or delegates,
  including `.worktrees/` and `.claude/worktrees/agent-*`. Delegate completion does
  not transfer that responsibility. Before ending the task, stop task-owned
  processes and remove its worktrees, disposable branches and dedicated Cargo
  target directories, subject to the preservation rules below. Never delete a
  shared target directory or a directory whose ownership is uncertain.
- Before removal, preserve the work through either a verified merge into the
  intended integration branch under the existing PR/merge gates, or a local
  archive. For an archive, commit only task-owned outstanding changes (including
  intended untracked files), run the required commit checks, and create a unique
  `archive/<worktree-name>-<timestamp>` tag at the final branch tip. Verify the tag

  overwrite an existing archive tag, include secrets/ignored build output, or
  discard unrelated edits to make cleanup succeed. Cleanup does not authorize
  merging, pushing, bypassing review or running `entire clean`.

  forced worktree removal, hard reset or bulk directory deletion to bypass a
  dirty worktree. Detached worktrees require the same preservation of their final

name: Scoped npm acceptance
on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      profile:
        type: string
        required: true
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  npm:
    name: Dependency acceptance
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 2
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: scope
        uses: ./.github/actions/ci-scope
        with:
          full: auto
      - name: Verify requested profile against exact merge
        env:
          EXPECTED: ${{ inputs.profile }}
          ACTUAL: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.profile }}
        run: |
          test "$EXPECTED" = "$ACTUAL"
          case "$ACTUAL" in help|frontend) ;; *) exit 1 ;; esac
      - name: Reserve browser cleanup time
        run: echo "MESH_UI_DEADLINE_MS=$(( $(date +%s) * 1000 + 28 * 60000 ))" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - name: Help MCP acceptance
        if: steps.scope.outputs.profile == 'help'
        run: |
          npm ci --prefix tools/help --ignore-scripts
          node --test tools/help/*.test.mjs
          npm run build --prefix tools/help -- --out "$RUNNER_TEMP/help-site"
          npm audit --prefix tools/help --audit-level=high
      - name: Frontend acceptance
        if: steps.scope.outputs.profile == 'frontend'
        working-directory: frontend
        run: |
          npm ci
          npm run lint
          npm run typecheck
          npm run test:coverage
          npm run build
          npm run check:build-syntax
          npm run audit:ci
      - name: Install representative browsers
        if: steps.scope.outputs.profile == 'frontend'
        working-directory: frontend
        run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium webkit
      - name: Chromium theme and layout regression
        if: steps.scope.outputs.profile == 'frontend'
        working-directory: frontend
        run: node ../scripts/ci/ui-runner.mjs e2e/ui-visual-regression.spec.ts e2e/theme-picker.spec.ts --workers=1 --retries=0 --reporter=list,../scripts/ci/ui-runner.mjs
      - name: WebKit portable regression
        if: steps.scope.outputs.profile == 'frontend'
        working-directory: frontend
        env:
          EVAL_BROWSER: webkit
        run: node ../scripts/ci/ui-runner.mjs --config=playwright.portable.config.ts --workers=1 --retries=0 --reporter=list,../scripts/ci/ui-runner.mjs
      - name: Preserve selected acceptance evidence
        if: ${{ always() && steps.scope.outputs.profile == 'frontend' }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: dependency-acceptance-${{ github.sha }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: |
            frontend/coverage/
            frontend/ui-runner-evidence/
            frontend/eval-results/
            frontend/test-results/
          retention-days: 7
          if-no-files-found: error

## Reliability before implementation

- Before implementing, refactoring, fixing or reviewing code, read the
  [AI coding reliability guide](docs/ai-coding-reliability.md), select the rules
  triggered by the changed boundaries, and inspect the owning code and callers.
  For concurrency/lifecycle changes, trace lock order, wait dependencies, actual
  work ownership, cancellation and commit authority before editing.
- Validate the applicable failure and recovery paths, not only the happy path.
  Record concrete evidence and remaining limits; a timeout, successful build or
  passing subset is not proof that UI freezes or all deadlocks are impossible.
- When a confirmed defect exposes a reusable failure pattern, update that guide's
  existing rule or add a distinct rule with its owner and regression evidence.
  Maintain the owning contract and test selectors; keep incident logs out of the guide.

## Project Structure & Module Organization

- Four-crate Rust workspace. `crates/mesh-talk-core/` is the UI-free protocol core (lib
  `mesh_talk_core` + the `mesh-talk-node` CLI bin in `src/bin/`): feature modules `node/`,
  `identity/`, `transport/`, `discovery/`, `eventlog/`, `ratchet/`, `channel/`, `dm.rs`,
  `file/`, `postoffice/`, `storage/`. `src-tauri/` is the Tauri desktop app: entry
  `src/main.rs` → `lib.rs`, IPC glue in `commands.rs` (auth) + `chat_commands/` (messaging)
  - `events.rs`, plus `state.rs`, `tray.rs`, `services/` (auth only).
- `crates/mesh-talk-integrations/` owns scoped local messaging grants, private IPC,
  and the dedicated bot host/admin CLI; `crates/mesh-talk-mcp/` adapts its four
  send/context/status tools to the official MCP SDK. Neither owns mesh crypto.
- Integration/e2e suites live in `crates/mesh-talk-core/tests/` (`two_node_cli`,
  `persistent_history`, `post_office_offline`, `decoder_smoke`); keep unit tests inline via
  `mod tests` (e.g. `node/node_tests.rs`).
- React client sits in `frontend/src`; Vite tooling in `frontend/package.json`.
- Operational scripts in `scripts/` (`setup-hooks.sh`, `check-health.sh`); architecture in
  `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`; conventions in `specifications/`. The
  [documentation map](docs/README.md) routes readers to maintained guides; the
  [documentation guidelines](docs/DOCUMENTATION_GUIDELINES.md) define ownership
  across the README, guides, and project site.

## Build, Test, and Development Commands

- `make dev` primes Rust + Node deps and installs git hooks.
- `make build` / `make frontend-build` — release build / Vite production build.
- During feature development, preview changed-boundary validation with `make test-plan`
  and run it with `make test-changed`. Unmapped changes require an explicit owner
  and reason; inspect escalation notes for browser/native or consumer checks.
  Use `make verify-plan` / `make verify-changed` at task completion to compose the
  same affected tests with applicable formatting, lint/types and builds. The
  test-only commands do not include static checks; neither mode replaces required
  PR/review, browser/native or release gates. `make validation-report` separates
  queue and execution costs; `make validation-audit` compares a clean affected
  plan with same-source broader failure evidence before narrowing any gate.
  Read selected capability references and inspect pending browser/native requirements.
  Execution prints a structured feedback report; follow the
  [validation protocol](docs/testing-feedback-loop.md#validation-stages-and-agent-responsibilities)
  for completed work, remaining evidence and additive semantic selections.
- During feature development, run affected tests only: `make test-focused
TEST_PACKAGE=mesh-talk-core TEST_FILTER=node::account_sync` selects Rust unit
  tests; add `TEST_TARGET=bridge_cross_lan` to select one integration target.
  `cd frontend && npm test -- src/features/chat/settingsDialogSession.test.ts`
  selects a frontend unit file. `make test` runs the full workspace suite
  (`cargo test --workspace`) for pre-PR and CI gates;
  `make e2e` runs the `#[ignore]`d multi-process backend rigs; `cd frontend && npm run e2e`
  runs the Playwright UI suite. Test builds use cheap KDF params (the `fast-test-kdf`
  feature), and `.cargo/config.toml` caps test/compile parallelism.
- UI / node spot checks: `make tauri-dev`, `make frontend-dev`,
  `cargo run -p mesh-talk-core --bin mesh-talk-node -- --keystore /tmp/a.keystore
--password pw --name alice` (add `--post-office` for relay mode).

## Coding Style & Naming Conventions

- Rust: `cargo fmt` (4-space, `snake_case` modules, `UpperCamelCase` types) +
  **`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`** (must match CI — `--all-targets` covers
  tests/benches).
- Frontend: `npm run format` (Prettier) + `npm run lint` (ESLint flat config).
- Write documentation and reusable prompts in English unless a specific exception is needed.
- Reference `specifications/development_conventions.md` for naming nuances.

## Domain Language

- `CONTEXT.md` is the canonical domain glossary. `docs/domain-design.md` indexes
  the modeling references and defines DDD vocabulary and naming translations.
- Distinguish local users, accounts and devices; desktop, transport and ratchet
  sessions; discovery, presence, custody, recipient delivery and read state.
- Use explicit identity/lifetime names in new code. Preserve public, wire and
  stored identifiers unless a separately validated compatibility change is intended.
- Update the glossary and affected owning guides when a domain meaning changes;
  link to definitions instead of maintaining duplicate glossaries.

## Architecture & Components

- Before adding business logic, consult [module ownership and reuse](docs/module-boundaries.md),
  inspect the owning module and its callers, and extend its existing implementation.
  Parallel tasks should name their owned paths and shared-interface dependencies;
  coordinate changes to shared interfaces through one integration owner. Keep
  feature-specific helpers local and share rules when their meaning and lifecycle
  are the same. The guide owns the detailed assignment and handoff contract.
- Stack: Rust 2024 on Tokio; Tauri 2 + React shell. No vendor-operated server.
- The `Node` (`node/node.rs`) wires identity + signed UDP **multicast** discovery
  (group `224.0.0.167`, port 47474) + Noise-encrypted TCP transport (`transport/`,
  low-level socket in `transport/net.rs`) + the content-addressed event log + DM/channel/
  file crypto. Messages are events synced as a bounded append-only log, account-addressed
  across a user's devices; optional offline custody via equal eligible post offices.
  Routed discovery and opt-in post-office federation connect reachable sites without
  joining their IP subnets. Wire formats are versioned bincode.
- See **`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`** before changing crypto, sync, or transport;
  **`docs/network-design-reference.md`** owns the communication invariants,
  module contracts, resource budgets and topology acceptance boundaries.

## Maintaining standards as requirements change

- Before changing tests, fixtures, dependencies or workflows in ways that affect
  CI cost or reliability, read [CI maintenance](docs/ci-maintenance.md). Reuse
  existing owners, measure the affected cost, and preserve acceptance evidence;
  keep required-check policy in its existing owner.
- Before implementation, identify the existing decision owner, authoritative rule,
  observable acceptance criteria, affected consumers and required boundary evidence.
  Extend the owning implementation and `validation.json`; new business capabilities
  should link their guide and invariants. Explain an unchanged contract in the PR.
- Run `make standards-check` after adding/moving source or changing contracts. It
  checks structural ownership and maintained references, including new files; it
  does not prove assertion quality, semantic completeness or candidate readiness.
  Hooks inspect the working tree, so partially staged commits still need a clean
  committed-candidate check in CI. Frontend dependencies must be installed.
- When CI exposes a local omission or flaky fixture, fix the owning selector, task
  or fixture and add a focused regression. Review timing and selection evidence
  before changing policy. Follow the maintained
  [requirement maintenance loop](docs/testing-feedback-loop.md#maintaining-standards-across-requirements).

## Testing Guidelines

- Integration coverage in `crates/mesh-talk-core/tests/` and `node/node_tests.rs`; embed
  unit tests near the code. Networking/crypto changes ship a loopback integration assertion.
- Backend multi-process E2E via `make e2e` (CI: `e2e-backend.yml`); Playwright UI E2E via
  `cd frontend && npm run e2e` (CI: `e2e-ui.yml`).
- Do not run full suites or E2E automatically during ordinary feature work. Run
  the affected unit or integration tests as changes are made; run E2E and the
  comprehensive health gate on explicit request, for optional full local preparation,
  or in CI.
- See `docs/testing-feedback-loop.md` for selection examples and escalation triggers.
- Document executed validation commands in every PR; ensure `make test` passes
  locally or through its matching CI workspace suite before merge.

## Commit & Pull Request Guidelines

- Before changing product versions or release automation, read [the version lifecycle](docs/updates.md#version-ownership-and-lifecycle).
  Root `Cargo.toml` `[workspace.package].version` is authoritative. Use
  `node scripts/release/version.mjs check|sync|prepare VERSION` (the `VERSION` argument belongs
  to `prepare` only); do not hand-edit generated npm/Cargo lock metadata or introduce another
  version constant. Root private npm metadata is a checked release-tooling projection;
  frontend private metadata is versionless and Tauri inherits Cargo. Never broadly replace
  matching dependency, fixture, history, wire or schema versions. Keep source builds `BASE-dev`,
  Nightlies `BASE-nightly.RUN.ATTEMPT`, official tagged builds `BASE`, and standard SemVer ordering.
- Version/changelog preparation and next-development-target changes use reviewed PRs. Ordinary main
  pushes must not create automatic release proposals or commit-derived product notes. Stable publication
  remains explicit through the existing verified tagged-release workflow; no direct main push,
  public empty release, mutable published tag or gate bypass. Nightly publication requires trusted
  `main` and a target above the latest Stable. Future changes must extend the existing version
  owner, its tests, standards/CI enforcement and capability contracts together; the owning guide
  documents permissions, bot-PR checks, dispatch and recovery requirements. Manual Stable draft
  preparation uses the reviewed exact-version CHANGELOG section and requires exact-source checks
  before creating its immutable tag/draft. The fixed release-history
  migration floor is historical provenance; never advance it during ordinary version bumps.

- Conventional commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`); scopes like `feat(node):` align with
  `specifications/git_standards.md`. Squash WIP; link issues. When asked to merge,
  default to squash merge unless the user explicitly requests another strategy;
  follow the [merge policy](specifications/git_standards.md#pull-request-merge-strategy)
  and current-head required checks.
- Create PRs through `./scripts/create-pr.sh -- <gh pr create options>`.
  The default checks the clean committed candidate, comparison base, argument safety,
  whitespace, cheap affected static checks, ownership blockers, structural standards,
  repository hygiene and applicable verified frontend patch coverage before publication.
  Use `make pr-check` for the same cheap static phase; missing current coverage
  evidence reports its explicit generation command and never starts suites implicitly.
  CI runs after publication; full-scope candidates retain cross-platform execution.
  Only the proven [documentation scope](docs/ci-maintenance.md#documentation-only-pr-scope)
  may omit unrelated product tests. All required checks must pass on the current PR head before merging. Creating a PR does not certify test acceptance.
- To run comprehensive checks locally before publication, use
  `./scripts/create-pr.sh --full-preflight <selectors/specs> -- <gh pr create options>`.
  This invokes `prepare-pr.sh` (platform preflight plus full health). For an existing
  PR, `./scripts/prepare-pr.sh <selectors/specs>` provides the same optional local gate.
  Use Playwright specs relevant to changed frontend behavior and repeated
  `--core-filter` / `--host-filter` / `--integration-filter` / `--mcp-filter` selectors
  for changed Rust crates. Preflight runs selected tests in Linux Docker and through
  SSH to `windows10`; Windows workspaces, caches and temporary data stay on drive D.
  Owning scenario rules add visual specs and require real native evidence for
  lifecycle/discovery changes. Missing environments or empty Rust selections fail
  full preflight. Include `e2e/ui-visual-regression.spec.ts` for theme/layout changes.
  See `docs/testing-feedback-loop.md` for configuration, coverage and plan preview.
  Fetch `origin/main` first if the comparison base is stale.
- Record focused validation and outstanding checks in the PR. Use
  `./scripts/check-health.sh` when comprehensive local evidence is needed; protected
  CI remains required before merge regardless of local results.

## Security & Adjustments

- `./scripts/check-health.sh` chains fmt, Clippy `--all-targets`, ESLint, tests, typos,
  cargo-deny, cargo-machete, gitleaks, shellcheck, audits, and both builds.
- Triage vulnerabilities immediately or document mitigation in the PR.
- If plans shift, update the relevant committed design or architecture docs. Keep
  `docs/superpowers/` and the root `plans/` directory local and untracked.

## Repository Hygiene

### Worktree lifecycle

- Create a worktree only when isolation is needed. Before creating one, inspect
  `git worktree list --porcelain` and record the task-owned path, branch and any
  dedicated build directory in ignored `tmp/` task notes. Treat pre-existing
  worktrees and unrelated changes as user-owned; never sweep them automatically.
- The coordinating session owns cleanup of every worktree it creates or delegates,
  including `.worktrees/` and `.claude/worktrees/agent-*`. Delegate completion does
  not transfer that responsibility. Before ending the task, stop task-owned
  processes and remove its worktrees, disposable branches and dedicated Cargo
  target directories, subject to the preservation rules below. Never delete a
  shared target directory or a directory whose ownership is uncertain.
- Before removal, preserve the work through either a verified merge into the
  intended integration branch under the existing PR/merge gates, or a local
  archive. For an archive, commit only task-owned outstanding changes (including
  intended untracked files), run the required commit checks, and create a unique
  `archive/<worktree-name>-<timestamp>` tag at the final branch tip. Verify the tag
  resolves to that tip and the worktree is clean before deleting anything. Never
  overwrite an existing archive tag, include secrets/ignored build output, or
  discard unrelated edits to make cleanup succeed. Cleanup does not authorize
  merging, pushing, bypassing review or running `entire clean`.
- Run removal from a surviving checkout with `git worktree remove <path>`, then
  `git branch -d <branch>` for a merged branch. Use `git branch -D <branch>` only
  for a task-owned archived branch after verifying its archive tag. Never use
  forced worktree removal, hard reset or bulk directory deletion to bypass a
  dirty worktree. Detached worktrees require the same preservation of their final
  commit before removal; there is no branch to delete.
- A pending PR, unresolved conflict, user decision, active concurrent session or
  failed preservation/cleanup step is an explicit retention exception. Preserve
  the required branch for an open PR; remove its clean worktree if no active work
  needs it. Recheck `git worktree list --porcelain` and task-owned branches/build
  paths before the final reply. Report cleanup performed and name every retained
  path/branch, its reason and the next action; never silently leave task worktrees.

- Keep implementation plans, research, investigation notes and scratch scripts
  under ignored `tmp/`; remove them when the work is complete.
- Merge durable decisions into the maintained owning guide. Do not commit
  completed-work reports, score histories, duplicate runbooks or archive copies.
- `docs/evals/` owns reusable suites/inventories, prompts and its README only.
  Generated evidence belongs in ignored output or PR/CI artifacts.
- Run `node scripts/check-repository-hygiene.mjs` before committing. The shared
  index check also runs in pre-commit, CI and health, rejecting ignored files
  even when force-added. See `docs/DOCUMENTATION_GUIDELINES.md` for ownership.

name: Dependabot auto-merge

on:
  pull_request_target:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review, edited]

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: dependabot-auto-merge-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  dependabot:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'dependabot[bot]'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      # Read metadata only. Never check out or execute the PR in this privileged workflow.
      - id: metadata
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request_target'
        uses: dependabot/fetch-metadata@25dd0e34f4fe68f24cc83900b1fe3fe149efef98 # v3
        with:
          github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - name: Classify auto-merge eligibility
        id: policy
        env:
          TARGET: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }}
          ECOSYSTEM: ${{ steps.metadata.outputs.package-ecosystem }}
          DIRECTORY: ${{ steps.metadata.outputs.directory }}
          UPDATE: ${{ steps.metadata.outputs.update-type }}
          NAMES: ${{ steps.metadata.outputs.dependency-names }}
          MAINTAINER_CHANGES: ${{ steps.metadata.outputs.maintainer-changes }}

          eligible=false
          if [ "$TARGET" = dev ] && [ "$ECOSYSTEM" = npm_and_yarn ] && [ "$MAINTAINER_CHANGES" = false ]; then
            case "$DIRECTORY" in
              /frontend|/tools/help)
                case "$UPDATE" in
                  version-update:semver-patch|version-update:semver-minor)
                    case "$NAMES" in
                      ''|*@tauri-apps/*) ;;
                      *) eligible=true ;;
                    esac
                    ;;
                esac
                ;;
            esac
          fi
          echo "eligible=$eligible" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Retain manual review for other updates
        if: ${{ always() && steps.policy.outputs.eligible != 'true' }}
        env:
          PR_URL: ${{ github.event.pull_request.html_url }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          enabled="$(gh pr view "$PR_URL" --json autoMergeRequest --jq '.autoMergeRequest != null')"
          if [ "$enabled" = true ]; then
            gh pr merge --disable-auto "$PR_URL"

test("auto-merge admits only known npm minor/patch metadata", async (t) => {
  const { mkdtempSync, readFileSync, rmSync } = await import("node:fs");
  const { tmpdir } = await import("node:os");
  const { join } = await import("node:path");
  const root = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "auto-merge-policy-"));
  t.after(() => rmSync(root, { recursive: true, force: true }));
  const valid = { TARGET: "dev", ECOSYSTEM: "npm_and_yarn", DIRECTORY: "/frontend", UPDATE: "version-update:semver-patch", NAMES: "jsdom", MAINTAINER_CHANGES: "false" };
  for (const [i, override] of [{}, { DIRECTORY: "/tools/help" }, { UPDATE: "version-update:semver-major" }, { ECOSYSTEM: "cargo" }, { NAMES: "@tauri-apps/api" }, { NAMES: "" }, { MAINTAINER_CHANGES: "true" }, { DIRECTORY: "/unknown" }, { TARGET: "main" }].entries()) {
    const file = join(root, String(i));
    const result = runGate("dependabot-auto-merge.yml", "Classify auto-merge eligibility", { ...valid, ...override, GITHUB_OUTPUT: file });
    assert.equal(result.status, 0, result.stderr);
    assert.equal(readFileSync(file, "utf8"), `eligible=${i < 2}\n`);
  }
  const source = read("dependabot-auto-merge.yml");
  assert.doesNotMatch(source, /actions\/checkout|skip-verification: true/u);
  assert.match(source, /gh pr merge --disable-auto/u);
  const revoke = step(source, "Retain manual review for other updates");
  assert.match(revoke, /if: \$\{\{ always\(\) && steps\.policy\.outputs\.eligible != 'true' \}\}/u);
  const job = workflowJob(source, "dependabot");
  assert.doesNotMatch(job.match(/^    if:.*$/mu)?.[0] ?? "", /base\.ref/u);

  assert.match(source, /--match-head-commit "\$EVENT_HEAD"/u);
});

test("auto-merge admits only known npm minor/patch metadata", async (t) => {
  const { mkdtempSync, readFileSync, rmSync } = await import("node:fs");
  const { tmpdir } = await import("node:os");
  const { join } = await import("node:path");
  const root = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "auto-merge-policy-"));
  t.after(() => rmSync(root, { recursive: true, force: true }));
  const valid = { TARGET: "dev", ECOSYSTEM: "npm_and_yarn", DIRECTORY: "/frontend", UPDATE: "version-update:semver-patch", NAMES: "jsdom", MAINTAINER_CHANGES: "false" };
  for (const [i, override] of [{}, { DIRECTORY: "/tools/help" }, { UPDATE: "version-update:semver-major" }, { ECOSYSTEM: "cargo" }, { NAMES: "@tauri-apps/api" }, { NAMES: "" }, { MAINTAINER_CHANGES: "true" }, { DIRECTORY: "/unknown" }, { TARGET: "main" }].entries()) {
    const file = join(root, String(i));
    const result = runGate("dependabot-auto-merge.yml", "Classify auto-merge eligibility", { ...valid, ...override, GITHUB_OUTPUT: file });
    assert.equal(result.status, 0, result.stderr);
    assert.equal(readFileSync(file, "utf8"), `eligible=${i < 2}\n`);
  }
  const source = read("dependabot-auto-merge.yml");
  assert.doesNotMatch(source, /actions\/checkout|skip-verification: true/u);
  assert.match(source, /gh pr merge --disable-auto/u);
  const revoke = step(source, "Retain manual review for other updates");
  assert.match(revoke, /if: \$\{\{ always\(\) && steps\.policy\.outputs\.eligible != 'true' \}\}/u);
  const job = workflowJob(source, "dependabot");
  assert.doesNotMatch(job.match(/^    if:.*$/mu)?.[0] ?? "", /base\.ref/u);

  assert.match(source, /--match-head-commit "\$EVENT_HEAD"/u);
});
name: Scoped npm acceptance
on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      profile:
        type: string
        required: true
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  npm:
    name: Dependency acceptance
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 2
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: scope
        uses: ./.github/actions/ci-scope
        with:
          full: auto
      - name: Verify requested profile against exact merge
        env:
          EXPECTED: ${{ inputs.profile }}
          ACTUAL: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.profile }}
        run: |
          test "$EXPECTED" = "$ACTUAL"
          case "$ACTUAL" in help|frontend) ;; *) exit 1 ;; esac
      - name: Reserve browser cleanup time
        run: |
          echo "MESH_UI_DEADLINE_MS=$(( $(date +%s) * 1000 + 28 * 60000 ))" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/dependency-browser"
          printf '%s\n' "$GITHUB_SHA" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/dependency-browser/source.txt"
      - name: Help MCP acceptance
        if: steps.scope.outputs.profile == 'help'
        run: |
          npm ci --prefix tools/help --ignore-scripts
          node --test tools/help/*.test.mjs
          npm run build --prefix tools/help -- --out "$RUNNER_TEMP/help-site"
          npm audit --prefix tools/help --audit-level=high
      - name: Frontend acceptance
        if: steps.scope.outputs.profile == 'frontend'
        working-directory: frontend
        run: |
          npm ci
          npm run lint
          npm run typecheck
          npm run test:coverage
          npm run build
          npm run check:build-syntax
          npm run audit:ci
      - name: Install representative browsers
        if: steps.scope.outputs.profile == 'frontend'
        working-directory: frontend
        run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium webkit
      - name: Chromium theme and layout regression
        env:
          MESH_UI_EVIDENCE_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/dependency-browser/chromium
        if: steps.scope.outputs.profile == 'frontend'
        working-directory: frontend
        run: node ../scripts/ci/ui-runner.mjs e2e/ui-visual-regression.spec.ts e2e/theme-picker.spec.ts --workers=1 --retries=0 --reporter=list,../scripts/ci/ui-runner.mjs
      - name: WebKit portable regression
        if: steps.scope.outputs.profile == 'frontend'
        working-directory: frontend
        env:
          EVAL_BROWSER: webkit
          MESH_UI_EVIDENCE_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/dependency-browser/webkit
        run: node ../scripts/ci/ui-runner.mjs --config=playwright.portable.config.ts --workers=1 --retries=0 --reporter=list,../scripts/ci/ui-runner.mjs
      - name: Preserve selected acceptance evidence
        if: ${{ always() && steps.scope.outputs.profile == 'frontend' }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: dependency-acceptance-${{ github.sha }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: |
            frontend/coverage/
            ${{ runner.temp }}/dependency-browser/
            frontend/eval-results/
            frontend/test-results/
          retention-days: 7
          if-no-files-found: error
"}
